Why it matters

Know what you’re working beside

Crocodiles are ambush predators that live in rivers, billabongs, estuaries and coastal waters across the north.

~100,000

estimated saltwater crocodiles in the wild in the Northern Territory

6 m

maximum length a saltwater crocodile can reach

Night

is when crocodiles are often most active — and hardest to see

Sources: Northern Territory Government (nt.gov.au) crocodile facts; University of Florida IFAS, Counting and Capturing Crocodilians.

How we control the risk

The CSA control ladder

We work down the ladder, starting with the least invasive control that keeps people safe. Capture sits at the bottom — it’s the last resort, not the default.

See our services
  1. 1AvoidMost preferred

    Plan the work away from the water’s edge: exclusion zones, timing, camp and access siting.

  2. 2Watch

    Dedicated spotters and overwatch with stop-work authority when crews must be near water.

  3. 3Train

    Toolbox talks and awareness training so every worker recognises and responds to the risk.

  4. 4RemoveLast resort

    Capture and relocation — only when other controls are impractical, and fully permitted.
